solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loud bird is cockerel perhaps

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A noisy bird turns out to be a crowing rooster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud bird' reads as one noisy creature, but Loud is the musical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is a young domestic cock, one example of poultry kept on farms.

clue.text: Predict change under Foreign Office

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting under another means it is written after it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for the Foreign Office
to recast is to change or remodel

explanation.surface: A civil servant anticipates reforms imposed by the Foreign Office.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast is to estimate in advance what will happen, a synonym of predict.

clue.text: Predator one across upset

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the answer to 1 across

explanation.surface: A predator troubles the bird from the across clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the answer at 1 across, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf is a carnivorous wild animal that hunts prey, so it is a predator.

clue.text: Strange couplet having eight parts

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd two-line verse that somehow has eight sections.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a couplet should have two lines, not eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Octuple means eightfold, consisting of eight parts or members.

clue.text: Seafood years in store going off

indicators.note: food going off is spoiling, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for years
taken as written

explanation.surface: Shellfish kept for years in a larder are turning bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' merely places the year inside the store before everything is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is a shellfish eaten as a delicacy, an example of seafood.

clue.text: Obliquely answer with poetry line in test

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the word for test

blocks.note: to try is to test
ANS is an abbreviation for answer
verse is poetry
L is short for line

explanation.surface: An exam question answered with a line of poetry, done in a roundabout way.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer, poetry and line chain together and then sit between TR and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Transversely means crosswise, lying across at an angle, which is to say obliquely.

clue.text: Royal at home caught by invading newspapers

indicators.note: invaders get inside a territory, so these letters go inside the word for newspapers

blocks.note: the press means newspapers collectively
someone at home is in
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A royal relaxing at home is snapped by intrusive tabloids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' reads as the royal being photographed, but caught is just the cricket abbreviation joining the home piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a female member of a royal family, so the noun royal fits.

clue.text: Thus it is seen in Oliver Goldsmith

indicators.note: something seen in a phrase sits visibly inside its letters

blocks.note: the end of the first name runs into the start of the surname

explanation.surface: A remark that a particular word appears in the writing of Oliver Goldsmith.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Goldsmith was an 18th-century Irish writer; his name just carries the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English to mean thus or consequently.

clue.text: Polite bore, chap needling everyone, initially looking embarrassed

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each preceding word

blocks.note: a well is a shaft bored into the ground
a chap is a man
first letters of these two words
someone embarrassed goes red

explanation.surface: A tedious man who annoys everyone ends up blushing despite his courtesy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a tiresome person, but here it is a noun for a drilled hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-mannered behaves with courtesy and good manners, which is being polite.

clue.text: Wheeling along, posh cars with monarch round centre of Bath

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the two in the middle
going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: Rollers is slang for Rolls-Royces
a king is a monarch
the two central letters of the city name

explanation.surface: Luxury cars and a monarch drive through the centre of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English spa city; an even-length word's centre is its middle two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Roller-skating means moving along on wheeled boots, so it is wheeling along.

clue.text: Whopper? Large, that is

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a whopper is a large one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whopper' looks like a description of size, but it is slang for a big untruth.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is informal for a blatant falsehood, a big untruth.

clue.text: General truth of maxim uncovered initially over minutes

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer wrapping is stripped away, losing the end letters
initially takes the first letter of each of the following words

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters
first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A general truth emerges from a maxim, revealed early on over a few minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as self-evidently true, a general truth or principle.

clue.text: Rum fellow, say, sporting red nails

indicators.note: sporting can mean playing about, so the letters are moved around playfully

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd chap is wearing red nail varnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the adjective for odd; it is Rùm, an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant of the Scottish isle of Rum is an example of someone living on an island.

clue.text: I arrive to travel round Mediterranean coast area

indicators.note: travelling round suggests moving about, so the letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tourist arrives to tour the Mediterranean coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is the stretch of Mediterranean shoreline in south-east France and north-west Italy.

clue.text: Person turning up ruined teen date

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shows up and spoils a teenager's date.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendee is someone present at an event, one who turns up.

clue.text: Stories about National Trust gifts

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: tales are stories
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust

explanation.surface: Tales of the National Trust receiving donations.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and land.
explanation.definitionFit: Talents are natural abilities, which are often called gifts.

clue.text: Dance quietly, Jimmy — and don't start with Jack

indicators.note: not starting with jack means the opening J, the card abbreviation, is dropped

blocks.note: sh is a call for quiet
the name loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone tells Jimmy to dance quietly and not begin with Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: The shimmy is a jazz-age dance involving shaking the body.

clue.text: Steer badly and turn back to starting point

indicators.note: badly steered, the letters go off course into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poor driver steers wrongly and has to go back to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset a device or counter is to return it to its initial state.

clue.text: The man's greeting son

blocks.note: hi is a greeting
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father welcomes his son.
explanation.definitionFit: His is the possessive pronoun meaning belonging to a male person already mentioned.

clue.text: Be attractive in drag

blocks.note: first meaning: to draw others towards oneself
second meaning: to haul something along

explanation.surface: Looking alluring while dressed as the opposite sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in drag' suggests cross-dressing, but drag here is the verb to haul.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb can mean exert magnetism or appeal, and also to tug or haul something along.

clue.text: Lowest part of car port

blocks.note: first meaning: the rubber ring touching the road
second meaning: the ancient Phoenician harbour city in Lebanon

explanation.surface: The underside of a car and a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: The rubber wheel covering is the bit of a vehicle meeting the road; Tyre is a Lebanese seaport.

clue.text: Mourned deeply, unfortunately little engaged?

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go wrong, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grieved deeply over a short-lived betrothal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' suggests betrothal, but means occupied in work; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Underemployed describes having too little work, being only slightly occupied.

clue.text: Sensationally and transparently when Charlie's king?

indicators.note: Charlie being king means the letter for Charlie is replaced by the letter for king

blocks.note: lucidly means clearly, transparently
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
R, rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style remark about a dramatic succession when Prince Charles became king.
explanation.walkthrough: The C in LUCIDLY swaps for R. The surface nods to Charles becoming king.
explanation.definitionFit: Luridly means in a shocking, vividly sensational way.

clue.text: In this establishment? In another establishment

indicators.note: the second In says the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Asked whether it happens here, the reply is that it happens elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves seem to contradict each other: one says this place, the other another place.
explanation.definitionFit: Here means at this place, so in this establishment is a fitting paraphrase.
